        "contents": "# Cursor Rules for miataru iOS App\n\n## Project Context\nThis is an open-source iOS application for privacy-friendly location tracking, sharing, and device management. Built with SwiftUI and modern iOS frameworks (iOS 18 and iOS 26).\n\n## Code Style &amp; Standards\n- Use SwiftUI best practices\n- Follow iOS Human Interface Guidelines\n- Maintain privacy-first approach\n- Use English for all code comments and strings\n- Implement proper error handling and battery optimization\n\n## Architecture Guidelines\n- Use ObservableObject and @Published for state management\n- Keep views lightweight and delegate business logic to managers\n- Implement proper MVVM pattern\n- Use UserDefaults for settings persistence\n- Handle location permissions gracefully\n\n## Key Components\n- LocationManager: Handles location tracking and permissions\n- SettingsManager: Manages user preferences\n- Device management and QR code functionality\n- Multi-platform support (iPhone, iPad, Mac)\n\n## Development Workflow\n- Test on multiple device types\n- Consider battery optimization\n- Maintain privacy compliance\n- Follow iOS app store guidelines\n\n## Common Patterns\n- Use @StateObject for view models\n- Implement proper onboarding flow\n- Handle background/foreground transitions\n- Manage device identifiers securely\n\n## Localization Guidelines\n\n### String Localization\n**ALWAYS** use &#96;NSLocalizedString&#96; for all user-facing text strings with proper English descriptions.\n\n#### ✅ Correct Implementation\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\nText(NSLocalizedString(\"no_groups_available_create_new\", comment: \"No groups available.         "contents": "### Accessibility\n- Provide meaningful labels for interactive elements\n- Use semantic colors and fonts\n- Test with VoiceOver and other accessibility features\n\n### Variable Naming\n- Use camelCase for variables and functions\n- Use descriptive names that explain the purpose\n- Avoid abbreviations unless they are widely understood\n\n## Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Copyright header is present and correctly formatted\n- [ ] All user-facing strings use &#96;NSLocalizedString&#96;\n- [ ] Proper error handling implemented\n- [ ] Memory leaks prevented (timers, publishers cancelled)\n- [ ] Code follows established naming conventions\n- [ ] Appropriate property wrappers used\n- [ ] Performance considerations addressed\n- [ ] Accessibility features implemented\n\n## Memories\n\n### Copyright Header Requirements\n- When new .swift files are created in the project, the cursor rules should automatically insert the standard copyright header. The date field in the header should always be set to the current date.\n\n### Commit Message Language\n- The user prefers commit messages to be written in English.\n\n### String Localization\n- The user prefers that all strings be implemented as NSLocalizedString with correct English descriptions.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [Apple Localization Guide](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/localization)\n- [SwiftUI Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui)\n- [iOS Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/ios)\n\n---\n\n**Remember**: Always prioritize user experience, maintainability, and code quality. When in doubt, follow the established patterns in the existing codebase.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "### Accessibility",
            "lineNumber": 213
          },

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 162
          },
          {
            "text": "**For developers:**",
            "lineNumber": 163
          },
          {
            "text": "- Localizations reside in &#96;en.lproj&#96;, &#96;de.lproj&#96;, and &#96;ja.lproj&#96;. Most text uses &#96;NSLocalizedString&#96; and SwiftUI accessibility modifiers to provide labels, hints, and traits.",
            "lineNumber": 164
          },
          {
            "text": "- Units adapt using the system &#96;measurementSystem&#96;. New strings (e.g., daily route‑limit reached) are provided in the string catalog for all supported languages.",
            "lineNumber": 165
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 166
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 167
          },
          {
            "text": "This document serves as a comprehensive reference for both users and developers of the miataru application.",
            "lineNumber": 168
          }
        ]
      },

        "contents": "# Cursor Rules for miataru iOS App\n\n## Project Context\nThis is an open-source iOS application for privacy-friendly location tracking, sharing, and device management. Built with SwiftUI and modern iOS frameworks (iOS 18 and iOS 26).\n\n## Code Style &amp; Standards\n- Use SwiftUI best practices\n- Follow iOS Human Interface Guidelines\n- Maintain privacy-first approach\n- Use English for all code comments and strings\n- Implement proper error handling and battery optimization\n\n## Architecture Guidelines\n- Use ObservableObject and @Published for state management\n- Keep views lightweight and delegate business logic to managers\n- Implement proper MVVM pattern\n- Use UserDefaults for settings persistence\n- Handle location permissions gracefully\n\n## Key Components\n- LocationManager: Handles location tracking and permissions\n- SettingsManager: Manages user preferences\n- Device management and QR code functionality\n- Multi-platform support (iPhone, iPad, Mac)\n\n## Development Workflow\n- Test on multiple device types\n- Consider battery optimization\n- Maintain privacy compliance\n- Follow iOS app store guidelines\n\n## Common Patterns\n- Use @StateObject for view models\n- Implement proper onboarding flow\n- Handle background/foreground transitions\n- Manage device identifiers securely\n\n## Localization Guidelines\n\n### String Localization\n**ALWAYS** use &#96;NSLocalizedString&#96; for all user-facing text strings with proper English descriptions.\n\n#### ✅ Correct Implementation\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\nText(NSLocalizedString(\"no_groups_available_create_new\", comment: \"No groups available. Create a new group to get started.\"))\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### ❌ Incorrect Implementation\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\nText(\"No groups available. Create a new group to get started.\")\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Localization Key Naming Convention\n- Use descriptive, lowercase keys with underscores\n- Follow the pattern: &#96;context_action_description&#96;\n- Examples:\n  - &#96;group_empty_add_devices_message&#96;\n  - &#96;no_groups_available_create_new&#96;\n  - &#96;edit_device&#96;\n  - &#96;delete_group&#96;\n\n### Comment Guidelines\n- Provide clear, descriptive English text in the comment parameter",

        "contents": "# miataru - App Store Description\n\n## Subtitle (30 characters max)\nYour Location, Your Control\n\n---\n\n## Description (4000 characters max) + Prompt\ntake this \"description text\" and translate these in this order: English, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, French, Italian, German, Japanese, Spanish, Simplified-Chinese \nOutput in this language order and make each language individually copyable markdown.Each copyable markdown portion has a small note of the language before the markdown and no markdown headline itself. It should be real markdown.\n\nDescription Text:\n\nTake control of your location sharing with miataru - the privacy-focused location sharing app that puts you in charge.\n\nmiataru is a powerful location tracking and sharing app designed for people who value privacy and control. Share your location with family, friends, or trusted devices through your own Miataru server, keeping your data secure and under your control.\n\nPrivacy First:\nYour location data belongs to you. miataru connects to Miataru servers that you choose, ensuring your location information never goes through third-party services you don't trust. You control who sees your location and when.\n\nSmart Location Tracking:\n• Background and foreground location sharing\n• Battery-optimized tracking that respects your device's power\n• High-accuracy updates when you need them, efficient monitoring when you don't\n\nMulti-Device Management:\n• Track multiple devices from a single app\n• Organize devices into custom groups for easy management\n• See battery levels, altitude, speed, and distance for each device\n\nBeautiful Maps &amp; Navigation:\n• Interactive maps with accuracy indicators\n• Real-time device positions with visual feedback\n• Off-screen arrows point to devices outside your current view\n• Built-in navigation with route planning and progress tracking\n\nEasy Sharing:\n• Generate QR codes to share your device instantly\n• Scan QR codes to add new devices quickly\n• Share via email, messages, or any app\n\nDesigned for iOS:",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "**For developers:**\n- &#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&#96; caches coordinates, manages a centralized reverse‑geocoding queue with a configurable distance threshold, and stores results in &#96;Application Support&#96;. Views consult the cache first before hitting the network and throttle UI updates to the configured map update interval.\n- Own‑device updates trigger immediate cache writes to kick off reverse geocoding promptly. A &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96; caches routes by device and transport, with distance‑based invalidation.\n- Static map elements such as &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96; and &#96;DeviceNameLabel&#96; are rasterized and cached with keys that include color scheme and display scale; renderers respect Dynamic Type and set &#96;isOpaque=false&#96; where appropriate.\n\n## Haptic Feedback and UI Enhancements\n**For users:**\n- Actions like successful refresh trigger subtle haptic feedback, pulsing accuracy circles show location precision, and shimmering indicators highlight loading states.\n\n- Animations for pulsing/shimmer are automatically reduced in Low Power Mode or when the app is backgrounded to save energy.\n\n**For developers:**\n- The &#96;Haptic&#96; utility abstracts platform differences. Shared UI elements such as &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96;, &#96;PulsingAccuracyCircle&#96;, &#96;Shimmer&#96;, &#96;MapCompass&#96;, and &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; reside under &#96;views/Common&#96; and are reused across device and group map views.\n\n## Multi‑platform Support\n**For users:**\n- The interface adapts to iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with platform‑specific root views and onboarding flows. iPhone uses a tab bar, iPad presents split views, and Mac currently mirrors the iPhone experience in a resizable window.\n\n- On iPad, you can open device details in separate windows for multitasking.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects the appropriate root view using size classes and platform checks. Dedicated onboarding containers exist for each platform, and many components in &#96;views/Common&#96; are platform agnostic.\n\n## Localization and Accessibility\n**For users:**\n- Available in English, German, and Japanese, with dynamic type and accessibility labels and hints applied to buttons, tab items, and swipe actions.\n\n- VoiceOver support has been improved across lists and map controls. Alerts and route‑limit messages are localized.",

        "contents": "- Data &amp; Caching:\n  - &#96;KnownDeviceStore&#96;, &#96;DeviceGroupStore&#96; (secure archiving under Application Support)\n  - &#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&#96; (latest device locations + reverse geocoded placemarks)\n  - &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96; (cached routes keyed by device/transport; distance threshold validation)\n- Utilities:\n  - &#96;thisDeviceIDManager&#96; (device ID generation + legacy migration)\n  - &#96;Haptic&#96; (feedback utilities)\n\n## 🔑 Key Features\n\n### Location Management\n- **Privacy-First**: User controls all location sharing\n- **Battery Optimized**: High-accuracy foreground; significant-change background\n- **Permission Handling**: Staged requests (WhenInUse → Always when opted-in)\n- **Background Support**: Significant-change updates\n\n### Device Management\n- **Multi-Device**: Track multiple devices\n- **Group Support**: Organize devices into groups\n- **QR Code Sharing**: Share own device, scan to add others\n- **Deep Link**: &#96;miataru://&lt;DEVICE_ID&gt;&#96; adds devices via sheet\n\n### User Experience\n- **Onboarding Flow**: Guided setup (iPhone/iPad-optimized)\n- **Settings Control**: Comprehensive preferences via SettingsManager\n- **Error Handling**: Transient overlays\n- **Localization**: German, English, and Japanese\n\n## 📱 Platform-Specific Considerations\n\n### iPhone\n- Touch-optimized interface\n- Location permission workflows\n- Deep-link and QR onboarding\n- Battery optimization features\n\n### iPad\n- Larger screen layouts\n- Split view support\n- Enhanced device management\n- Optimized for productivity\n\n### Mac\n- Not currently targeted (Mac directory hosts onboarding previews only)\n\n## 🛠️ Development Guidelines\n\n### Code Organization\n- **Views**: Minimal UI logic, delegate to managers\n- **Managers**: Handle business logic and data\n- **Models**: Use SwiftUI data binding\n- **Assets**: Organized by platform and feature\n\n### State Management\n- Use ObservableObject for view models\n- Implement proper MVVM pattern\n- Handle app lifecycle changes\n- Manage user preferences reactively\n\n### Testing Strategy\n- Unit tests for business logic\n- UI tests for critical flows",

        "contents": "# miataru iOS App - Project Overview\n\n## 🎯 Project Purpose\nmiataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups. The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\n\n## 🏗️ Architecture Overview\n\n### Technology Stack\n- **Frontend**: SwiftUI (iOS 18.0+)\n- **State Management**: ObservableObject pattern with @Published properties\n- **Data Persistence**: UserDefaults via SettingsManager; Application Support files for devices/groups\n- **Location Services**: CoreLocation framework (foreground and significant-change background)\n- **QR Code**: CodeScanner (scan), QRCode (generate)\n- **Platforms**: iPhone and iPad\n\n### Core Components\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmiataruApp.swift (Entry Point)\n├── MiataruRootView (Main Navigation)\n├── OnboardingContainerView (User Setup)\n├── LocationManagers/\n│   └── LocationManager.swift\n├── SettingsManagers/\n│   └── App Settings/ (SettingsManager, thisDeviceIDManager, Settings.bundle)\n│   └── Devices/ (KnownDevice, KnownDeviceStore)\n│   └── Groups/ (DeviceGroup, DeviceGroupStore)\n├── views/\n│   ├── Common/ (Shared UI)\n│   ├── iPhone/ (iPhone-specific)\n│   ├── iPad/ (iPad-specific)\n│   └── Mac/ (onboarding previews only)\n└── Assets/ (Resources &amp; Localization)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Common Components Overview\n\n- Shared UI (&#96;views/Common/&#96;):\n  - &#96;ErrorOverlay&#96;, &#96;ViewModifiers&#96; (adaptive toolbars/navigation)\n  - Device &amp; group UI: &#96;DeviceRowView&#96;, &#96;GroupRowView&#96;, &#96;DeviceNameLabel&#96;, &#96;DeviceBatterySymbol&#96;\n  - Map UI &amp; helpers (&#96;views/Common/Map/&#96;): &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96;, &#96;PulsingAccuracyCircle&#96;, &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; (+ &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96;), &#96;MapCompass&#96;, &#96;OffScreenDeviceArrow&#96;, &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96;, &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96;, &#96;RouteStyle&#96;, &#96;Shimmer&#96;\n- Data &amp; Caching:\n  - &#96;KnownDeviceStore&#96;, &#96;DeviceGroupStore&#96; (secure archiving under Application Support)",

        "contents": "# Development Guide - miataru iOS App\n\n## Quick Start for Developers\n\n### Prerequisites\n- Xcode 16.0+ (iOS 18.0+ deployment target)\n- iOS 18.0+ device or simulator\n- Swift 5+\n- macOS 14.0+ (for development)\n\n### Setup\n1. Clone the repository\n2. Open &#96;miataru/miataru.xcodeproj&#96; in Xcode\n3. Select your development team in project settings\n4. Build and run on target device/simulator\n\n## Project Structure Deep Dive\n\n### Core Architecture\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmiataru/\n├── miataruApp.swift          # App entry, global state, onboarding &amp; deep links\n├── views/                    # UI components\n│   ├── Common/               # Shared UI elements\n│   ├── iPhone/               # Root, devices, groups, settings, QR\n│   ├── iPad/                 # Root, devices, groups, settings\n│   └── Mac/                  # Onboarding previews (no Mac target)\n├── LocationManagers/         # Location handling (fg/bg, significant-change)\n├── SettingsManagers/         # User preferences &amp; data stores\n│   ├── App Settings/         # SettingsManager, Settings.bundle\n│   ├── Devices/              # KnownDevice, KnownDeviceStore\n│   └── Groups/               # DeviceGroup, DeviceGroupStore\n└── Assets/                   # Resources &amp; localization (xcstrings, icons)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Common Components Overview\n\n- Shared UI (&#96;views/Common/&#96;):\n  - &#96;ErrorOverlay&#96; (transient errors), &#96;ViewModifiers&#96; (&#96;adaptiveToolbarBackground&#96;, &#96;adaptiveNavigationBackground&#96;)\n  - &#96;DeviceRowView&#96;, &#96;GroupRowView&#96;, &#96;DeviceNameLabel&#96; (label caching), &#96;DeviceBatterySymbol&#96;\n  - Map helpers (&#96;views/Common/Map/&#96;): &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96;, &#96;PulsingAccuracyCircle&#96;, &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; + &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96;, &#96;MapCompass&#96;, &#96;OffScreenDeviceArrow&#96;, &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96;, &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96;, &#96;RouteStyle&#96;, &#96;Shimmer&#96;\n- Stores &amp; caches:\n  - &#96;KnownDeviceStore&#96;, &#96;DeviceGroupStore&#96; (secure archiving to Application Support)",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# Development Guide - miataru iOS App",
            "lineNumber": 1
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2
          },
          {
            "text": "## Quick Start for Developers",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4
          },
          {
            "text": "### Prerequisites",

          {

          {
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "## Project Structure Deep Dive",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "### Core Architecture",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",

          },
          {
            "text": "miataru/",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "├── miataruApp.swift          # App entry, global state, onboarding &amp; deep links",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "text": "├── views/                    # UI components",
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "│   ├── Common/               # Shared UI elements",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "text": "│   ├── iPhone/               # Root, devices, groups, settings, QR",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "text": "│   ├── iPad/                 # Root, devices, groups, settings",
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "text": "│   └── Mac/                  # Onboarding previews (no Mac target)",
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "├── LocationManagers/         # Location handling (fg/bg, significant-change)",
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "text": "├── SettingsManagers/         # User preferences &amp; data stores",
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "text": "│   ├── App Settings/         # SettingsManager, Settings.bundle",
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "text": "│   ├── Devices/              # KnownDevice, KnownDeviceStore",
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "text": "│   └── Groups/               # DeviceGroup, DeviceGroupStore",
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "text": "└── Assets/                   # Resources &amp; localization (xcstrings, icons)",
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "### Common Components Overview",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "- Shared UI (&#96;views/Common/&#96;):",
            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
            "text": "  - &#96;ErrorOverlay&#96; (transient errors), &#96;ViewModifiers&#96; (&#96;adaptiveToolbarBackground&#96;, &#96;adaptiveNavigationBackground&#96;)",
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {
            "text": "  - &#96;DeviceRowView&#96;, &#96;GroupRowView&#96;, &#96;DeviceNameLabel&#96; (label caching), &#96;DeviceBatterySymbol&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {
            "text": "  - Map helpers (&#96;views/Common/Map/&#96;): &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96;, &#96;PulsingAccuracyCircle&#96;, &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; + &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96;, &#96;MapCompass&#96;, &#96;OffScreenDeviceArrow&#96;, &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96;, &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96;, &#96;RouteStyle&#96;, &#96;Shimmer&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 41
          },
          {
            "text": "- Stores &amp; caches:",
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "text": "  - &#96;KnownDeviceStore&#96;, &#96;DeviceGroupStore&#96; (secure archiving to Application Support)",
            "lineNumber": 43
          }
        ]
      },

        "contents": "### Accessibility\n- Provide meaningful labels for interactive elements\n- Use semantic colors and fonts\n- Test with VoiceOver and other accessibility features\n\n### Variable Naming\n- Use camelCase for variables and functions\n- Use descriptive names that explain the purpose\n- Avoid abbreviations unless they are widely understood\n\n## Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Copyright header is present and correctly formatted\n- [ ] All user-facing strings use &#96;NSLocalizedString&#96;\n- [ ] Proper error handling implemented\n- [ ] Memory leaks prevented (timers, publishers cancelled)\n- [ ] Code follows established naming conventions\n- [ ] Appropriate property wrappers used\n- [ ] Performance considerations addressed\n- [ ] Accessibility features implemented\n\n## Memories\n\n### Copyright Header Requirements\n- When new .swift files are created in the project, the cursor rules should automatically insert the standard copyright header. The date field in the header should always be set to the current date.\n\n### Commit Message Language\n- The user prefers commit messages to be written in English.\n\n### String Localization\n- The user prefers that all strings be implemented as NSLocalizedString with correct English descriptions.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [Apple Localization Guide](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/localization)\n- [SwiftUI Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui)\n- [iOS Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/ios)\n\n---\n\n**Remember**: Always prioritize user experience, maintainability, and code quality. When in doubt, follow the established patterns in the existing codebase.",

        "contents": "- Unit tests for business logic\n- UI tests for critical flows\n- Multi-device testing\n- Permission flow verification\n\n## 🔒 Privacy &amp; Security\n\n### Data Protection\n- Location data encryption\n- User consent requirements\n- Data retention policies\n- GDPR compliance\n\n### Permission Management\n- Minimal permission requests\n- Clear permission explanations\n- Graceful permission denial\n- User control over data\n\n## 📊 Performance Considerations\n\n### Battery Optimization\n- Smart location updates\n- Background task management\n- Auto-lock control\n- Energy-efficient operations\n\n### Memory Management\n- Proper observer cleanup\n- Weak reference usage\n- Resource deallocation\n- Memory leak prevention\n\n## 🚀 Deployment &amp; Distribution\n\n### Build Requirements\n- Xcode 16.0+\n- iOS 18.0+ deployment target\n- Swift 5+\n- macOS 14.0+ (development)\n\n### Distribution\n- App Store distribution\n- TestFlight beta testing\n- Enterprise deployment support\n- Universal binary support\n\n## 🔧 Common Development Tasks\n\n### Adding Features\n1. Create platform-specific views\n2. Implement business logic in managers\n3. Update settings if needed\n4. Add localization strings\n5. Test on all platforms\n\n### Debugging\n- Location simulation in Xcode\n- Permission status checking\n- Battery usage monitoring\n- Background task verification\n\n### Performance Tuning\n- Instruments profiling\n- Memory usage analysis\n- Battery impact assessment\n- Background task optimization\n\n## 📚 Resources &amp; References\n\n### Documentation\n- [SwiftUI Documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui)\n- [CoreLocation Framework](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corelocation)\n- [iOS Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines)\n\n### Dependencies\n- **CodeScanner**: QR code scanning\n- **MiataruAPIClient** (via local &#96;Libraries/MiataruClientSwift&#96;): API client\n- **QRCode**: QR generation\n- **SwiftImageReadWrite**: Image handling\n\n## 🎯 Future Roadmap\n\n### Planned Features\n- Enhanced privacy controls\n- Advanced device grouping\n- Improved battery optimization",

        "contents": "### Comment Guidelines\n- Provide clear, descriptive English text in the comment parameter\n- Use proper English grammar and punctuation\n- Make the comment self-explanatory for translators\n- Avoid technical jargon in comments\n\n### Adding New Localized Strings\n1. Add the &#96;NSLocalizedString&#96; call in your Swift code\n2. Add the key-value pair to &#96;Localizable.xcstrings&#96;\n3. Provide translations for all supported languages (en, de, ja)\n\n## File Naming Conventions\n\n### Directory Structure\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmiataru/\n├── views/\n│   ├── iPhone/\n│   ├── iPad/\n│   ├── Mac/\n│   └── Common/\n├── LocationManagers/\n├── SettingsManagers/\n└── Libraries/\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### File Naming\n- iPhone views: &#96;iPhone_ViewName.swift&#96;\n- iPad views: &#96;iPad_ViewName.swift&#96;\n- Mac views: &#96;Mac_ViewName.swift&#96;\n- Common/Shared views: &#96;ViewName.swift&#96;\n- Group related files in descriptive directories\n- Use clear, descriptive names for files\n- Follow the established pattern for platform-specific views\n\n## Copyright Header Requirements\n\n### Mandatory Copyright Header\n**ALWAYS** add the following copyright header to the top of every new Swift file:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\n/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * [FileName].swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on [CurrentDate].\n */\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### ✅ Correct Implementation\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\n/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * MyNewView.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 2025-01-25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n// ... rest of the file content\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### ❌ Incorrect Implementation\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\nimport SwiftUI\n// Missing copyright header\n// ... rest of the file content\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Header Guidelines\n- Place the header at the very top of the file, before any imports\n- Replace &#96;[FileName]&#96; with the actual filename (e.g., &#96;MyNewView.swift&#96;)\n- Replace &#96;[CurrentDate]&#96; with the current date in format YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., 2025-01-25)\n- Keep the exact copyright text and format\n- The header must be the first content in every Swift file",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "### Comment Guidelines",

          {
            "text": "- Provide clear, descriptive English text in the comment parameter",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./APP_FEATURES.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 28
          }
        },
        "contents": "# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\n\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\n\n## App Navigation and Views\n**For users:**\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\n\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;iPhone_RootView&#96; constructs the &#96;TabView&#96; and hosts &#96;iPhone_DevicesView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_GroupsView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96;, and &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96;.\n- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects platform‑specific root containers so iPad and Mac can embed their own navigation styles.\n- iPad supports opening device detail windows using a value‑based &#96;WindowGroup(for: String)&#96; and context menu/drag interactions.\n\n## Location Tracking\n**For users:**\n- Enable background and foreground tracking in *Settings* to share your location with a Miataru server.\n- The app sends updates even with the screen locked and records a log of recent updates.\n- Location sharing can store history on the server and works offline until network connectivity resumes.\n- Tracking accuracy, activity type, and sensitivity are configurable in *Settings*, and a \"Location Tracking Details\" page shows the last GPS and server updates.\n\n- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\n- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;LocationManager&#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &#96;MiataruAPIClient&#96;.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide",
            "lineNumber": 1
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2
          },
          {
            "text": "This document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.",
            "lineNumber": 3
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4
          },
          {
            "text": "## App Navigation and Views",
            "lineNumber": 5
          },
          {
            "text": "**For users:**",
            "lineNumber": 6
          },
          {
            "text": "- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.",
            "lineNumber": 7
          },
          {
            "text": "- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.",
            "lineNumber": 8
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 9
          },
          {
            "text": "- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.",
            "lineNumber": 10
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 11
          },
          {
            "text": "**For developers:**",
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;iPhone_RootView&#96; constructs the &#96;TabView&#96; and hosts &#96;iPhone_DevicesView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_GroupsView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96;, and &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects platform‑specific root containers so iPad and Mac can embed their own navigation styles.",
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "- iPad supports opening device detail windows using a value‑based &#96;WindowGroup(for: String)&#96; and context menu/drag interactions.",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "## Location Tracking",
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "text": "**For users:**",
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "- Enable background and foreground tracking in *Settings* to share your location with a Miataru server.",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "text": "- The app sends updates even with the screen locked and records a log of recent updates.",
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "- Location sharing can store history on the server and works offline until network connectivity resumes.",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "- Tracking accuracy, activity type, and sensitivity are configurable in *Settings*, and a \"Location Tracking Details\" page shows the last GPS and server updates.",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "text": "- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "text": "**For developers:**",
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;LocationManager&#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &#96;MiataruAPIClient&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 28
          }
        ]
      },

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * KnownDeviceStore.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport Foundation\nimport UIKit\nimport Combine\n\n// Falls erforderlich, KnownDevice importieren (bei getrennten Modulen):\n// import miataru\n\nclass KnownDeviceStore: ObservableObject {\n    static let shared = KnownDeviceStore()\n    \n    @Published var devices: [KnownDevice] = [] {\n        didSet {\n            guard !isInitializing else { return }\n            setupSubscribers()\n            save()\n            WidgetDataSyncCoordinator.syncAllDevices()\n        }\n    }\n    private let fileName = \"knownDevices.plist\"\n    private var cancellables: [AnyCancellable] = []\n    private var isInitializing = true\n\n    private var fileURL: URL {\n        AppDirectories.applicationSupportFile(named: fileName)\n    }\n\n    // Make init private for singleton\n    private init() {\n        self.devices = load()\n        // Sicherstellen, dass das eigene Gerät immer in der Liste ist\n        let myDeviceID = thisDeviceIDManager.shared.deviceID\n        if !self.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == myDeviceID }) {\n            let myDeviceName = NSLocalizedString(\"my_device\", comment: \"Name for the user's own device in the device list\")\n            let myDevice = KnownDevice(name: myDeviceName, deviceID: myDeviceID, color: UIColor.systemBlue)\n            self.devices.insert(myDevice, at: 0)\n            debugLog(\"[DEBUG] Eigenes Gerät mit DeviceID \\(myDeviceID) wurde automatisch als erstes Device hinzugefügt.\")\n            save()\n        }\n        setupSubscribers()\n        isInitializing = false\n    }\n\n    private func setupSubscribers() {\n        cancellables = []\n        for device in devices {\n            ",

Alle Übersetzungen sind korrigiert. Zusammenfassung:

## Zusammenfassung der Änderungen

**Deutsch (3 Stellen korrigiert):**
1. "öffnen Sie bitte... gewähren Sie... Ihren Standort" → "öffne bitte... gewähre... deinen Standort"
2. "Ihr Standort" → "dein Standort"
3. "zu Ihnen... von Ihnen" → "zu dir... von dir"

**Französisch (alle formalen Formen korrigiert):**
- "vous/votre/vos" → "tu/ton/ta/tes" in allen benutzerbezogenen Texten
- Beispiele: "Vous pouvez" → "Tu peux", "votre appareil" → "ton appareil", "Vos données" → "Tes données"

**Spanisch und Italienisch:**
- Bereits durchgehend informell (tú/usted korrekt verwendet, Italienisch verwendet bereits "tu/ti/tuo")

Alle Übersetzungen verwenden jetzt durchgehend die informelle Anrede (Du/tu) für Sprachen, in denen das anwendbar ist. Die Änderungen wurden in der Datei `Localizable.xcstrings` gespeichert.
